277: Pelhřimov Festival of Records and a corporate event
278: Today we broke our record for the number of riders deployed (not counting side programmes at trade fairs). Vlasta, Martin Šimůnek, kids from the club and Tobík Dolák went on bikes to the Festival of Records in Pelhřimov, which was celebrating its founding anniversary. On a motorbike there was Dalibor Šulc, plus parkour athletes Ondra and Honza from Flow Vision. Lukáš Valný and Michal Budský were busy at a corporate event in Žatec.
279: The festival itself nailed the weather, and in almost 28 degrees records were broken all day, concerts took place and you could try out lots of attractions. Our team was placed right next to the main stage, and our task in 3 main 40-minute  shows was both to perform and to set new Czech records. We left the first show without records but made it longer. In the second show Vlasta Kabeláč Čiháček and Honza Daleký set a record in the standing long jump – Honza with feet together and Vlasta from back wheel to back wheel between two obstacles. Together that gave the guys 5.6 metres in the final attempts. Honza also set a standing jump record for parkour. Vlasta didn't beat his existing Czech record.{1}The last, shortest show at the end of the event was dedicated to Dalibor Šulc's record attempt: he set a Czech record for spins on the back wheel – 6 spins on the spot on the back wheel in 36 seconds.{2}We gave the shows our all and unfortunately not without injuries. First, parkour athlete Ondra broke a metatarsal bone in his foot, but neither the spectators nor the rest of us noticed anything until he started complaining about pain in his foot. Our youngest rider, Márty Kabeláč, fooled around on the back wheel for so long that he hit his nose and left an indelible pool of blood on Pelhřimov square. But by the last show he was back on the bike. Among other things, there was also a workshop for visitors.

282: Martin Šimůnek in Milovice and Struhařov
283: When everyone on the team is on holiday, Martin keeps riding. An indestructible rider who, even on the threshold of 50, manages several exhibitions a week plus rides in the bike park or on the trails around Česká Lípa – and on top of that he's a multiple national and world champion. This time Martin stood in for the guys, who were on a well-deserved holiday, at the local children's day in Milovice and in Struhařov – close to traditional Trial and MTB spots.
284: A few photos from Struhařov have just arrived, so take a look at how Martin still jumps.
286: Unfortunately we don't often get the chance to ride exhibitions in the home town of our club, MTB & Trial Mraveniště Říčany.
287: Unfortunately we don't often get the chance to ride exhibitions in the home town of our club, MTB & Trial Mraveniště Říčany. So we were all the more eager to accept the invitation from the organisers of the Busking and Food Festival on Říčany square, and at the same time the offer to promote the Bikefestival in Tehov, which we are organising on 25/26 June. As it's a festival of street art and food, we also tested our portable sound system with a microphone, which extends our team's ability to perform even without sound provided by the organiser.
288: The exhibition was ridden by Vlasta Kabeláč Čiháček and Matouš Balík, who showed the people of Říčany a slightly higher level of Trial. There was some extra egging on over volunteers and riding on the traditional steps by the church after the exhibition. Thanks to all the locals for your support :)
289: The first Bikeskills camps – mission accomplished
290: For the first time in the history of our project we tried starting the camp season in April. We cancelled the first date because of snow and debated whether to keep the 28–29 April date too. We can only thank our participants for their flexibility – after looking at the Sunday forecast, they agreed to move to the Saturday date.
291: Our coaches were able to cover both the men's and the women's group and make full use of the beautiful Sunday weather. The men threw themselves into the terrain and natural features in the beautiful Struhařov forests, while the ladies focused on technique in the Tehov park before moving to the nearby trails.
292: Thanks to everyone for taking part and for your willingness. Hopefully you'll notice the improvement on every ride this year.

301: The slightly tabloid headline of this report literally reflects the type of events our team took part in.
302: First up were the European Marathon Championships, with Vlasta Kabeláč Čiháček and Martin Šimůnek, who besides the main exhibition at the opening ceremony also rode at the local school for almost 300 pupils, including a small workshop. On the square there was a slight delay to the ceremony itself, but the spectators cheered all the more even in the rising heat.
304: Forestry Days is a traditional event where over 15,000 people head to the middle of the forest to admire forestry machinery, hunters' trophies and everything connected with the forest and its care. Martin Šimůnek, Dominik Budský and Vlasta Kabeláč Čiháček could already feel the approaching heat right behind their ears, but they still rode a relatively brisk exhibition on the STIHL Timbersports stage, including jumping over champion lumberjacks. Pack up and head for the furnace of Česká Lípa …
306: During the day the centre of Česká Lípa welcomed literally thousands of people, who enjoyed both the nearby fair and attractions and the main stage, where a number of well-known bands performed. Scorching heat of over 32 degrees and an asphalt surface aren't exactly ideal for drawing people in, but our team still managed to fill the square. Martin Šimůnek, Vlasta, Dominik Budský (unicyclist) and Matouš Balík were joined by local Trial legend and Martin's first student Majkl Matys, who got his Trial bike out after many years and showed that some things you never forget. Thanks partly to his help the heat was bearable, and together with Vlasta they pulled off big ones over the tape along with the competitors. Four generations of Trial riders effectively had a chance to meet at the exhibition.
308: Without Michal and Dominik, our team headed to Liberec for an event for a few hundred enthusiastic handball players. Luckily the exhibition was aimed at the after-party, held outdoors and in the shade. The heat had caused one of the ramps onto the obstacles to crack at the previous exhibitions, and the riders were showing a certain amount of fatigue too. But the crowd of enthusiastic athletes gave us energy, and with help from the club's little ones Marty and Nikolka Kabeláč, a 30-minute show got going that entertained kids and adults alike. Matouš Balík seemed the freshest of all – he even won the mini contest in the tape jump. We got home well after 10, but full of experiences.
310: A traditional event for Martin Šimůnek and something new for Vlasta as a guest rider. The big North Bohemian cycling race impressed with the quality of its organisation, its side programme and above all more than 900 registered riders. The pleasant surroundings of the Rumburk centre also attracted countless spectators, who together with the riders created a nice backdrop for our exhibition.
311: We coped with the smaller space and stretched the exhibition out a bit. We also invited a young gun from the crowd, who had ridden the race as a Junior but caught the Trial bug at the workshop and managed a few basic moves. Thanks for the invitation to this 39th edition – and here's to the 40th.
312: Women Tune Up with Bikeskills – Šembera trails
313: This weekend, and Friday too, was a bit more demanding. Getting used to the coaching pace and organising events after Covid is tough, but the results are worth it. On Friday and Saturday Vlasta had individual coaching in Tehov, while Mára, Lukáš and Katarína with Matouš taught skill-hungry women and girls on the Šembera trails. In the individual courses the main goal was learning to jump benches. Surprisingly, everyone who came – even though it didn't look like it at first – fought hard and sent the benches at full commitment.
314: So far we've also collected positive reactions about the camp. The Šembera trails are aimed more at families and kids, but you can still find a few things there where a rider can learn something and fine-tune their style. Some riders found the trail profile just right for them, while others would deserve harder, more demanding sections.
315: You keep bombarding us with interest in a camp during or after the summer holidays. We'll try to prepare a few dates, but given our Trial exhibitions it will take some time. It should be clear in the first week of July :){1}{2}Next weekend, "btw", you can see us at {3}www.vsenakolech.cz{4} in Kostelec or in Prostřední Bečva in Moravia.
316: Houpačka Festival – charity exhibition in Velešín
317: Another interesting festival took place in Velešín. Unfortunately, because of traffic Vlasta and Lukáš arrived late and had to battle against time to get everything done. We opened the whole event and were the opening act for the invited bands. Lots of attractions and music performances attracted a relatively large number of spectators even at the start, who came to watch our exhibition too, which we squeezed into about 25 minutes including a competition for volunteers. Thanks for the invitation – next time we'll try to arrive earlier :)
318: Bike park testing and smaller weekend exhibitions
320: The Friday farewell for kids at the camps in Petrohrad is ridden every year by Martin Šimůnek, but he was called away by family commitments and it was up to Vlasta to stand in for him. What could be better than taking along the smallest rider from the club, Marty, to ride a show with his dad for participants of the same age or older?
321: The sun was scorching a bit, but after the exhibition we still held a small workshop for those interested, lending bikes to an estimated 40–50 kids, including competitions.
322: {1}23/7 – Test camp and exhibition at Polevsko bike park – Polevsko near Česká Lípa{2}
323: We needed to thoroughly test the Polevsko bike park for possible camps in 2023, and the Saturday coaching event with a Trial exhibition, to which Martin and Vlasta were invited, was the ideal chance to ride the whole park to the full. Club rider Petr Jeřicha used the spare seat in the car to train for the Enduro Series, and despite the bad forecast set off with Vlasta to meet Martin and host Michal Matys.
324: Apart from a few morning drops, luckily it didn't rain until 3 pm, so we managed to coach a small group of bikers, ride 2 short exhibitions and do some photography. We went through the tricky parts of the local trails and the bike park's options and rode the local chairlift. For us, Polevsko is a nice family bike park with technique, jumps and a few small drops. Its 4 trails will soon be extended by an almost 8 km trail, but even in their current state, with multiple lines and hidden jumps, they'll keep every biker entertained.
325: We look forward to next year and a possible Bikeskills camp or coaching.
327: One of this year's longest trips to an exhibition, to Vyšní Lhota, was made by Vlasta Kabeláč Čiháček, Tobík Dolák and Marty Kabeláč. The interesting setting attracted a few hundred spectators, who partied at the concerts despite the sweltering heat, and our exhibition was really an adrenaline addition to a rock afternoon and evening.
328: In two shows they rode both a classic exhibition and a show with egging on for bigger jumps and competitions for spectators. The local hospitality is definitely worth a mention too – we hadn't been so stuffed between exhibitions for a long time.
330: Ball Lightning 1 – Great-Grandpa's Tractor and Písek near Jablunkov
331: Michal Budský and Mára Tryner made a proper Moravian trip, going from north to south. The first stop was a children's day in Písek near Jablunkov, where they started their exhibition on the team's folding obstacles.
332: Meanwhile Martin Šimůnek was running a workshop at a children's day in Hradec Králové, and Vlasta and Matouš set off for the traditional Great-Grandpa's Tractor event in Čáslav. Every year you can see loads of historic machinery, a programme for kids and adults, and occasionally more extreme things like our show. The guys rode two shows – the first to warm up and the second at full throttle for a decent number of spectators, who weren't put off even by the heat radiating from the melting asphalt.
333: Mělník festival, forest days in Ralsko and Javornice day
334: Another weekend in full swing. On Friday we were busy at the Mělník festival in Podolí park, which moved from the Mělník riverside. Two shows with 5 riders in a pleasant park setting were great. We also tested our new obstacle setup a bit more and new dual headset microphones for bigger events where we need two hosts. The spectators came to enjoy the event, so we could stretch out every show. Our obstacles were then used by the parkour athletes too. Martin Šimůnek once again proved that choosing volunteers is his weak point, when for the sideways jump he picked a local athlete who drew with Vlasta in the first show and blew him out like a candle in the athlete-vs-bike duel in the second.
